assumptions_and_risks: Planner inspected immutable input/base source, live issue56 and PR65 plus saved issue46 shared acceptance; issue body matches immutable original. No builds/probes/tests run during planning.
Detached planner submodules are absent; populate/reuse exact pinned dependencies in each build setup, recording source/path/SHA. Do not claim dependency/configuration errors as test evidence.

Master cleanup may legitimately SIGKILL still-live siblings after loss. Initial-fault barrier chooses an ordering where the healthy sibling has already exited and been reaped, allowing the original exact-success oracle to remain strict. Existing #13 held-sibling/mixed-order cases independently cover cleanup ordering.

Use Linux GCC/Clang compatible linker wrapping, CMake/CTest/Ninja (or an explicitly recorded generator), Python3 and subreaper/process-group support. Tool paths and role placeholders must be concretized and intent-published before execution.

Events are PIPE_BUF-sized atomic writes; injection scoping excludes controller/library calls. pthread_sigmask returns an error number; dup2 uses -1/errno. Verify no barrier deadlock and unconditional group cleanup even on baseline failure.
A successful recovery here is a deterministic pre-runtime no-progress crash followed by real complete replacement work; it does not claim real GPU crash recovery or successful prefix reuse.
All required failed/skipped/unavailable/incomplete gates block acceptance; native Windows exclusion does not become a passing platform claim.

original.requirement:
## Problem

In the fork-child branch of bool ProcessProgress::start_child_process, failed pthread_sigmask or dup2 returns EXIT_FAILURE. On the audited platform EXIT_FAILURE is 1, converted to true. The failed child can return into controller code after closing its controller descriptors instead of terminating.

## Evidence level

Independently checked source-proven conditional branch. No actual pthread_sigmask/dup2 failure was injected during the audit; the consequences depend on the failing call and remaining slots.

## Reproduction / verification status

Source inspection: follow the return statements at Linux controller lines 576–578 and 605–609 back to the initial/recovery Boolean callers. Proposed regression: inject each child-only setup failure, assert child exit, no controller fallthrough and no child-created extra workers. That injection has not yet been run.

## Required outcome and acceptance

- Every post-fork fatal child setup error takes a terminal child-exit path, never a Boolean return into parent/controller execution.
- Inject each covered failure and assert process tree, cleanup/reaping, parent status and absence of unintended worker spawning.
- Audit neighboring child-return branches and use child-safe termination semantics. Keep rare fault branches distinct from ordinary launch behavior.

## Scope and references

Fix/investigate the lifecycle boundary described above, including its regression coverage. Do not expand this into Steam scheduling policy, automatic deployment, a general scheduler rewrite or unrelated Vulkan behavior.

## Shared acceptance and evidence

This is a child of the worker lifecycle epic through GitHub's native hierarchy. Its shared verification/compatibility gates apply. Add deterministic assertion-bearing regression coverage that fails before the fix where feasible; retain healthy controls. These research probes expose defects and are not passing product tests.

Audit source: `556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec`; local audit baseline `2325a40846cceb9e053cc5b26aad4c030e07e1a2`. The relevant platform supervisor/owner headers remain unchanged in fork master `5eb2c496dde819c868fa3d7d1e52c51047d9adb8`. No claim is made about Steam's installed version, report frequency, or hardware cache behavior.
